comments.value:
On an LTS release there would be nothing blocking from an update. However, the only reason to update is if any of the fixes will have any significant impact to the game. Otherwise there is no reason to update until the 2018 LTS version is released.

Also how and where would you be using raycasting without custom scripting in vrchat? Why did you specifically link that fix?

Additionally I see nothing in the LTS releases 16-19 that would benefit vrchat. I mean it wouldn't hurt to update as long as they clarify the unity versions in the sdk better.

@{5ab3ad272b67505f726c2a8f|full_name}: because it's a pretty big part of the engine. There's actually a ton of things I could have linked to, but that's just one huge example that I imagine is used a lot on the packages that vrchat uses. (Physics: Fixed RaycastHit.textureCoord performance issue, was internally copying whole mesh index buffer for no good reason) A ray is fired into the Scene. The textureCoord is the location where the ray has hit a collider. RaycastHit._textureCoord is a texture coordinate when a hit occurs - this causes a massive memory leak over time. This is probably a fairly large bit of performance regression. they also fixed a JobTempAlloc memory leak and random crash when rendering a scene with a SpriteRenderer when using Graphics Jobs - and many maps use sprites, they fixed an issue that now allows you to use shaders from 2017.2 assetbundles... etc etc.

@{5a60e3832478a072c83fa7ce|full_name}: I dont think you understand how specific these fixes are. They may sound big but in most cases are not related and or unless the application is experiencing these issues there is little incentive to update.

You can keep listing things you think are related to vrchat if you want and ill go through them with you:
- RaycastHit.textureCoord has a very specific use case and restricted to mesh colliders. vrchat uses primitive colliders and UI menus for interaction that I can test. only custom worlds can use mesh colliders and creators dont have access to the texture coord as far as im aware. so this most likely only be found in official maps where they can use custom scripts, if it is used at all.
- using asset bundles from 2017.2 means nothing as vrchat moved to 2017.4 from 5.6 and the game now only accepts asset bundle uploads from those two versions of unity.
- the graphics jobs is a patch from 2018.3.4 which means if they are using the experimental feature my bets are on waiting for  the 2018 LTS because if spriteRenderers are indeed causing a crashes this needs to be reported with the appropriate world link as it nowhere near a common issue right now. You find one of the many worlds you think are using spriterenderers and not textured quads or ui images, then ill help test.

@{5ab3ad272b67505f726c2a8f|full_name}: thanks for the clarification - but one clarification from me: I've only copied things from LTS releases, not 2018.3.4. The issue with asset bundles is related to what USERS might use or try to use in the unity editor when making avatars and worlds in unity, not what gets bundled and sent to vrchat. Sprites? check rogue shadow's worlds, at one point at least he was using a sprite sheet animation for his dancer. I was concerned that people's avatar animation overrides could potentially contain some of the things causing memory leaks as well. Correct me if I'm wrong, but RaycastHit.textureCoord could potentially be used in shaders and shaderphysics, and I thought that raycasthit was used for interaction with controllers and gaze all over vrchat (though not necessarily on the UI.) Less specifically, many people have experienced slowdowns on this version of the unity editor generally speaking, and many of the bug fixes improve stability of the unity editor, and while not directly connected to vrchat, it would be nice for the users to have a more stable and current LTS build, particularly the one that is current in unity hub rather than a previous build that unity themselves considers deprecated.

@{5a60e3832478a072c83fa7ce|full_name}: 
- LTS builds address crashes, regressions, and issues that are found in future TECH releases. ie the fix from 2018.3.4 was added to one of the 2017 LTS releases. 
- So many things in unity use sprites but not everything can be done with a spriterenderer in vrchat. You would need to know if rogue is animating the sprite sheet manually, using a shader, or using particles before being concerned about the bug. As for avatars its always possible but try and find someone using a 2D avatar, that is even using the spriterenderer, in a public world vs 3D model. Its not concerning enough to worry about
- a user cant load an asset bundle. an asset bundle in unity is typically downloaded during gameplay. ie when your client downloads an avatar or world, those are asset bundles. Thus it is not an issue that we or vrchat need to care about. Dont get them confused with unity packages
- I already corrected you on the textureCoord. Thats a very specific usage of a raycast that serves no purpose for navigating and selecting. This is everything you can get from a raycastHit in unity (https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/RaycastHit.html). The impact point is the most useful. Raycasting with physics requires custom scripts which is something not possible by creators so there is no concern there.
- Youre going to need to be specific with what people are referring to slowdowns. The only current issues I know about are the vrchat sdk causing editor lag due to some functions that run whenever the inspector is updated.
- The unity editor is actually more stable than you might think for anyone creating for vrchat. Creators are not working or will not run into  99% of the editor fixes that the newer builds address. You would need to point out an editor fix that you think all creators might benefit from. 
- side note a new LTS build was released, 20f1. Still nothing for vrchat from what I can see though

@{5ab3ad272b67505f726c2a8f|full_name}: I'm satisfied with that answer, thanks for addressing some of the concerns around the later lts builds being available and at looking into it. There's another thread posted recently by members of the animation community around "general slowdowns" that seem to have an effect on the performance for the local player (not remote viewers/other players) with particles along with cloth simulations (likely due to virtual particles), and more specifically I was curious if it was tangentially related to the engine itself. I suppose you would have to try the 20f1 build to see if the local performance issues are less pronounced with the test avatars they provided.

@{5a60e3832478a072c83fa7ce|full_name}: Those issues are more likely game related in terms of how vrchat has implemented the various activation and syncing methods. A clear sign pointing towards it being vrchat's fault right now and not the engine is how it only affects the client that activates it rather than everyone seeing the same effect. You were originally referencing editor slowdowns which can be different from in game slowdows but in this case vrchat appears to have broken something in the latest update. In addition there are slowly more issues being reported regarding the latest 2019.1.1 vrchat update.

no problem, I hope this conversation helps clears up a few things regarding why they dont just jump into updating. but who knows they could turn around tomorrow and update to unity 2019 beta if they wanted, I have no control over what they do or what they are thinking. In fact nobody really knows what they are thinking, the communication from development is so bad, we dont even know if our feedback is being acknowledged in any way.
Thank you for reporting this issue. However, since the post is quite old and hasn't been updated recently, we encourage you to create a new ticket if the problem still persists.

details:
Fixed in unity 2017.4.17f1 and https://issuetracker.unity3d.com/issues/raycasthit-dot-texturecoord-is-very-slow
There are a lot of bug fixes in the january 28th release of unity, and I'm not entirely sure there's many stopping/blocking differences between 15f and 19f1. I think some crashes being seen lately in the bug reports are related. 
I think keeping up with unity 2017.4's builds might help things a lot, there's a lot of performance related issues on the build we're on.
title: Unity physics, RaycastHit.textureCoord performance hit.
